item.title: 'What I have learnt is that I should not think so much ahead': Prithvi Shaw prefers to stay in the present
item.description: KOLKATA: Prithvi Shaw showed glimpses of his vintage best as he led Maharashtra to a 10-wicket victory against Bengal in the Ranji Trophy Elite Group ‘C’ match at the Eden Gardens here on Thursday. The opener got his second half-century in this Ranji season to stay unbeaten on 53 off 50 balls while striking three fours and four sixes during his innings. However, Shaw preferred not to look too far ahead but stay in the present. “What I have learnt from experience is that I should not think so much ahead,” he said. “Like I am giving an interview now. After this, I will go to the room and then think about what to do. I don’t think more than that. Just keep winning games. Have good training. Eat well,” he said, laying down his programme. The 26-year-old last played for India five years ago and would definitely look to make a return to the national side. “There is always that thought at the back of the mind. But now I do not think so much ahead,” he explained. His immediate challenge is to put together a consistent run of scores in domestic cricket. The explosive opener has hit two half-centuries in seven innings this Ranji season, with his highest score of 70 coming against Delhi in Maharashtra’s opening match. Since then, he has scored 7, 21, 0, 17 and 12. “Some innings will go bad and some will go well. There is no problem with my start. Big runs are just a matter of one innings,” he felt. Shaw is enjoying leading Maharashtra after shifting from Mumbai last season. “I feel Mumbai and Pune are not too far apart. There is a difference of 1.5 to 2 hours, and I know a lot of players. Ritu (Gaikwad), Ankit (Bawne) here. So I never felt that I have come far from home. I am very comfortable, and have enjoyed it a lot,” he said. The opener enjoyed facing experienced pacer Mohammed Shami. “Shami Bhai is bowling as he used to. There is no change. He is bowling fast. It was about how to play Shami Bhai well because I feel he is the main bowler for such wickets,” he said.

item.title: Glendale's Joelle Rover shows maturity beyond his years after viral moment seen by millions
item.description: SPRINGFIELD — The country was introduced to the Southside Showdown on Oct. 8. Glendale defeated Kickapoo 35-6, but the game was never the story. Glendale wide receiver Joelle Rover was grabbed by referee Kevin Elmer following a touchdown. Millions saw the incident on social media. Influential accounts, including former NFL quarterback and Heisman Trophy winner Robert Griffin III, shared the video. “It’s just like football. Bad plays happen, bad stuff happens,” Rover said. “You just need to move on from it and go to the next play, next opportunity. From that instance, a lot of opportunities have opened up to me.” While MSHSAA has suspended Elmer, Rover’s reaction and maturity were the most striking. Rover never complained and didn’t react negatively in the moment. He said he’s quite proud of it, telling the News-Leader last week. High school football: MSHSAA suspends referee after incident in Glendale game “I can’t say that I’m grateful for what happened,” Rover said. “But I’m grateful for how I acted in the situation.” Rover hasn’t received an apology or been in contact with Elmer. But other Missouri high school referees have sent him messages of support. “They’ve congratulated me on my character. I really appreciated that,” Rover said. “It’s a thing that they didn’t have to and they did it anyways. I’m grateful for that.” During Glendale’s win over Rolla, Rover jogged back to the line of scrimmage to start a new play. A Rolla player was overheard asking him about the referee incident, saying he'd seen the video on TikTok. Rover took it in stride and kept playing. After millions of people know who Rover is, it would be easy for him to succumb to the pressure and not perform. Instead, the wide receiver and defensive back has risen to the challenge. High school football: How Trevor Heman has become one of Missouri's all-time great wide receivers The senior has 727 receiving yards and a team-high 13 touchdowns. His composure and willingness to do anything for the team despite the incident have made head coach Frank Tristan really proud. “Joelle hasn’t changed. He’s a happy-go-lucky, consistent guy,” Tristan said. “The way he has handled this hasn’t surprised me at all. It’s probably why he is a phenomenal three-sport athlete. In some games, the stands will be just screaming at him and he will just keep playing.” Rover and Glendale have a big district semifinal game on the road against Helias Catholic on Friday, Nov. 6. Liam Keating covers high school sports and Missouri State athletics for The Springfield News-Leader. item.title: Colby Covington killed his RAF aura with embarrassing loss to Raul Rosas Jr. — ‘He’s supposed to beat Khamzat?’
item.description: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - DECEMBER 16: Colby Covington of the United States enters the octagon for a welterweight title fight against Leon Edwards of England during the UFC 296: Edwards vs. Covington event at T-Mobile Arena on December 16, 2023 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Sean M. Haffey/Getty Images) | Getty Images Colby Covington provides a great argument for exclusive contracts. “Chaos” is scheduled to wrestle former UFC middleweight champion Khamzat Chimaev atop the RAF Abu Dhabi fight card later this month in UAE, a matchup that had a certain amount of intrigue after Covington dominated Arman Tsarukyan at RAF 11 back in July. Then Covington went and got submitted by UFC bantamweight prospect Raul Rosas Jr. at Hype Italy less than two weeks before his Chimaev showdown, which pretty much killed his aura and left longtime critics ( like this former champion ) laughing their asses off. “He gets f*cking taken down, double-legged, this is the whole fight, 40 seconds,” retired UFC bantamweight and current RAF headliner Henry Cejudo said on his Pound 4 Pound podcast with Kamaru Usman. “Look at this motherf*cker, and he’s supposed to beat Khamzat Chimaev next f*cking week? Colby Covington, you ain’t the king of sh*t no more. This does hurt. I guess people will get over it. If he’s able to come out and beat Khamzat Chimaev, people will forget it, or maybe he’ll get a rematch with Raul Rosas, but I think Raul will probably do that shit again to him.” Covington is currently ranked No. 1 in the promotion . “First and foremost, I would say this: That’s not excusable because of your name and the brand that you’ve built,” Usman added. “It’s not excusable. Now us, real fighters and competitors, we know how difficult and how different they are. Super different. Wrestling and jiu-jitsu are completely different. So Raul Rosas caught him off guard, got in there, and put him away. You could see [Covington’s] face. He was not ready for that level of intensity right away. For a guy that’s supposed to be intense, he was not ready for that level of intensity.” Time for the “king” to surrender his crown?

item.title: Ole Miss and the College Football Playoff roadmap
item.description: BATON ROUGE, LOUISIANA - SEPTEMBER 05: A detailed view of the CFP logo on a Clemson equipment case during the second half of a game at Tiger Stadium on September 05, 2026 in Baton Rouge, Louisiana. (Photo by Tyler Kaufman/Getty Images) | Getty Images As we know by now, our Ole Miss Rebels have debuted at No. 10 in the initial College Football Playoff rankings. Last season was the only year the Rebels have made the playoffs and they debuted at No. 6 and never dropped below No. 7. Some important things to note as we explore the path for Ole Miss is the one and two loss teams they are ahead of and the two loss teams they are behind. Alabama and Texas are ahead of Ole Miss with two losses of their own. Texas has the head-to-head victory while Bama was one of the more puzzling placements. The tide have a home loss to Georgia and an ugly road loss against Tennessee. Texas has a really bad loss to Oklahoma and a home loss to Florida. The Rebels have the blowout road loss (with context) to Florida and a road loss, with injuries, to Texas. So Ole Miss is the only one not to lose at home of the three. What is important to note is that a 7-1 BYU team is only one spot ahead and 8-0 UCLA is just two spots ahead. One loss by either of those schools will mean a lot. The standings directly behind the Rebels looks like this: 11. Notre Dame (7-1) 12. Ohio State (6-2) 13. Tennessee (6-2) 14. LSU (6-2) 15. Texas Tech (7-1) 16. Wake Forest (7-1) 17. Houston (6-2) 18. Missouri (6-2) The CFP Roadmap Route 1: Pretty straight forward, win out and win the SEC Championship and likely receive a bye. Route 2: Win out but not be in the SEC title game (Texas vs Bama), and host a first round game. Route 3: Lose to anyone not named Georgia and all hope is gone. Route 4: “Quality loss” to Georgia. So don’t get blown out. This is where we will spend the time looking at how a loss to Georgia isn’t the end: Georgia finishes 11-1 and wins the SEC Championship. (Still have to play Mizzou and South Carolina). Kentucky loses two more games, preferably to Louisville and Florida. Also have Tennessee and Missouri remaining. UCLA dropping two games. They have to travel to Minnesota and Michigan while hosting Illinois and USC. BYU loses to Utah Notre Dame loses to Miami Florida wins out Tennessee to beat LSU but lose to Texas A&M LSU beats Bama but loses to Tennessee Missouri is a wild card in all of this because of their potential to rack up some big resume wins. They play Texas, Georgia, Kentucky and Oklahoma. Their next three games are against current top 7 teams. If they win two of those and beat Oklahoma, the head-to-head may be the only thing saving Ole Miss at that point, especially since it was dominant. I am not saying all of these things MUST happen, but if we happen to drop the Georgia game, these things would go a long way to keeping hope alive!

item.title: Warriors Withhold $20 Million From Porzingis In Ugly Saga
item.description: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images The New York Knicks are facing a complex situation involving Kristaps Porzingis. The Golden State Warriors have stopped sending money to Porzingis. They say he is not playing, so he does not get his $20 million salary. NBA insider Shams Charania reported this on Tuesday. The move makes an already ugly situation much worse for the big man. He is dealing with a mystery illness and might quit the league for good. New York fans can only watch this drama unfold from the other side of the country. The Cost of an Empty Roster Spot The Warriors are holding back cash and trying to dump the contract, leaving the Knicks to navigate the fallout. Charania noted that the team can move his deal before the Feb. 11 deadline. They want a rival to take on the salary so they can save money. “Absorbing Porzingis’ near-expiring deal would allow a rival team to move a salary out and save money and clear a roster spot via a buyout,” he continued, according to the New York Post . No one wants a player who might retire and costs that much. The Knicks do not need this headache, but the league might have to swallow it. Steve Kerr’s Close Call in New York While Porzingis fights for his paycheck, Steve Kerr is looking back at a chance to coach in New York. Kevin Durant confirmed that Kerr almost took the job years ago. The Knicks had a deal on the table when Phil Jackson was running the show. Kerr stayed in California for his family. He told NBA.com that turning down Phil was hard. “Ultimately, it was agonizing to say no to Phil because of what I think of him and what he’s done for my career,” Kerr said, according to Yardbarker . He knew the job would be a huge challenge far from home. A Young Prospect Gets Cut Meanwhile, the Knicks made their own tough choice on Monday. The team decided not to pick up the option for Pacome Dadiet. Not picking up the option for Pacome Dadiet saves $5.4 million for the 2027-28 season. Dadiet is a 21-year-old from France who has played very little. He only appeared in one game so far this season. The Knicks declined the option, and he will be a free agent soon. This move clears a spot for someone who can actually play. It shows the front office is willing to cut ties when the results do not match the draft pick.

item.title: Duran a Silver Slugger finalist
item.description: MINNEAPOLIS, MN - SEPTEMBER 25: Ezequiel Duran #20 of the Texas Rangers bats during the game between the Texas Rangers and the Minnesota Twins at Target Field on Friday, September 25, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Michael Turner/MLB Photos via Getty Images) | MLB Photos via Getty Images Texas Rangers jack of all trades Ezequiel Duran is a finalist for the Silver Slugger Award for utility players, it was announced today. Duran is up against the Tigers’ Kevin McGonigle and Sam Antonacci of the White Sox. Duran, who already won the Gold Glove for the utility player spot this offseason, slashed .260/.320/.419 this season, good for a 114 OPS+, and also was 12 for 16 on stolen base attempts. He played all over the diamond for the Rangers, with 49 starts at shortstop, 41 starts at third base, 20 starts in the outfield, 25 starts at second base, and one start at first base. McGonigle, who made his major league debut this season, led American League position players in bWAR this year at 7.1 bWAR. He split his time roughly evenly between shortstop and third base, and slashed .278/.376/.430, good for a 126 OPS+. Antonacci is a rather baffling finalist here. He started 109 games this season in left field and 13 games at second base, although he did appear in another 19 games at second base that he didn’t start. Still, he seems like a left fielder who occasionally played second base rather than a utility guy. He slashed .277/.370/.396, good for a 116 OPS+. item.title: Bronny James added to CV Lakers roster, but will he play Friday?
item.description: The Los Angeles Lakers announced Thursday that they have assigned Bronny James as well as first-round draft pick Cameron Carr to the Coachella Valley Lakers. The CV Lakers make their debut on Friday night against the Salt Lake City Stars at Acrisure Arena at 7 p.m. A team spokesman said it is still to be determined whether James, the son of basketball icon LeBron James, will play for the CV Lakers on Friday or if it is a logistical move sometimes necessary between a G League team and its parent team. Bronny James and Carr are scheduled to be with the CV Lakers when they practices at Acrisure Arena on Thursday afternoon. Bronny played six games for the South Beach Lakers during the 2025-26 season averaging 9.5 points in those games. He has played at Acrisure Arena before, famously taking the court with his father LeBron for the first time during an exhibition game in the desert in 2024. item.title: Panthers’ Brad Marchand drops updated injury timeline amid left knee injury
item.description: Ed Mulholland-Imagn Images Panthers’ Brad Marchand drops updated injury timeline amid left knee injury appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Florida Panthers are still navigating injuries on their team this season, and Brad Marchand is one of the players who’s currently dealing with something. The forward has been out since Oct. 6 after getting injured against the Los Angeles Kings. At the time, the Panthers said that he’d be out for six weeks, but it looks like he’ll be back sometime in December . “I can’t say it’s this month, but probably within five weeks, six weeks,’’ Marchand said via George Richards of NHL.com. “I’ve never been so happy to be out for this amount of time.” For Marchand, that’s good news, as he thought it was going to be longer until he was able to return to the ice. item.title: Shaw becomes Ferguson's first Glentoran signing
item.description: Shaw joins Glentoran on a deal until the end of the season [Getty Images] Duncan Ferguson has made his first signing as Glentoran boss, bringing in English winger Nathan Shaw on a deal until the end of the the season. The 25-year-old has been training with the Glens and joins the club after a spell at Scottish Championship side Greenock Morton. Shaw, who can operate on the left and the right, came through Blackpool's academy and made four appearances for the first team. He also had loan spells at Bamber Bridge, AFC Fylde and Stockport County before joining Flyde permanently. A move to Scotland with Inverness then followed and Shaw scored 10 goals in his first season at the club as they reached the 2023 Scottish Cup final, and he started against Celtic at Hampden Park decider. He then joined Morton in June 2024 and made 62 appearances across two seasons before departing earlier this year. Shaw said he "jumped at the chance" to join Glentoran after Ferguson made contact. "The opportunity to join a club like Glentoran and be part of what he wants to achieve here really appealed to me," he added. "I've been here for the past couple of weeks, and that's made me even more certain this is where I want to be. You quickly get a sense of how big the club is, how much it means to people and the expectation to compete for trophies. "You can see how determined Duncan is to bring success here. He's putting the hours in and is very hands-on in training. He'll stop a session, show you what he wants and work through it until everyone understands their job and how he wants the team to play. "Everything I've seen tells me the club is geared towards success. I want to play my part by creating chances, scoring goals and helping the team win. I know I have to earn my place, and I'm determined to do that."

item.title: Vasiliy Lomachenko Signs Multi-Year Deal With Top Rank Boxing
item.description: What To Know After 16 months out of the ring, Vasiliy Lomachenko, one of boxing’s most accomplished athletes, will return. Lomachenko has re-signed with his original promoters at Top Rank Boxing and is expected to have his first fight on February 13. Lomachenko, age 38, wants to achieve the one goal that has eluded him: becoming an undisputed world champion. It’s official. Vasiliy Lomachenko is back home at Top Rank. The Ukrainian three-division world champion and two-time Olympic gold medalist recently discussed ending his 16-month retirement and made it official on Wednesday. Lomachenko and Top Rank announced a multi-year co-promotional agreement through his newly formed Loma Power Promotions . Lomachenko announced his retirement in June 2025. item.title: Everton Eye £35m Defender: Should Moyes Trigger His Clause?
item.description: Everton Eye £35m Defender: Should Moyes Trigger His Clause? Everton have given themselves a promising platform under David Moyes, sitting seventh in the Premier League after nine matches with 13 points. Three wins, four draws and two defeats have kept the Toffees firmly in the European conversation, while consecutive victories against Newcastle United have strengthened their momentum, including an EFL Cup quarter-final place. Sustaining that progress will require more defensive depth, particularly with several players carrying important responsibilities. Ainsley Maitland-Niles, signed during the summer to provide experienced defensive cover, has established himself as a prominent right-back option and remains contracted until June 2029. Jake O’Brien offers another alternative through 2028, while Jarrad Branthwaite and James Tarkowski have deals running until 2030. Michael Keane, however, reaches the end of his contract in June 2027. Keane’s situation gives Everton another reason to consider defensive succession planning. Moyes values defenders who maintain physical intensity, protect their positions and adjust between a conventional back four and a three-man defence. A younger player with those qualities could reduce the pressure on experienced starters without disrupting the current structure. Sport Witness reports that Everton, Newcastle United and Fulham enquired about Celta Vigo defender Javi Rodríguez in August, with Bournemouth joining the competition. The 23-year-old Spaniard offers precisely the versatility Moyes appreciates, operating at right-back or on the right of a defensive trio. Rodríguez has recorded three goals and one assist across his first 10 competitive appearances in 2026/27, adding attacking contribution to his defensive responsibilities. Yet Celta Vigo have secured him until June 2030 and insist they won’t sell key players in January. His £35m release clause represents the only straightforward route to forcing a departure, while Rodríguez himself has described Celta as the club of his life. Should Everton trigger Rodríguez’s £35m clause in January? VIGO, SPAIN – APRIL 16: Javi Rodriguez of RC Celta Vigo controls the ball during the UEFA Europa League 2025/26 Quarter-Final Leg Two match between Real Club Celta and SC Freiburg at Estadio Balaidos on April 16, 2026 in Vigo, Spain. (Photo by Diogo Cardoso/Getty Images) Everton should resist that temptation. Rodríguez’s versatility and technical composure make him an attractive long-term option, particularly with Keane’s contract approaching its final months. Still, paying £35m upfront for a player who wants to remain in Spain would create unnecessary financial pressure under the Squad Cost Ratio rules. The Friedkin Group must protect the progress Moyes has achieved, rather than compromise squad stability for an expensive January gamble. Maitland-Niles and Tarkowski can cover the immediate requirements, allowing Everton to revisit Rodríguez during summer negotiations.

item.title: Max Verstappen responds to Toto Wolff’s claim that era of "ruthless" F1 drivers is over
item.description: Motorsport photo Four-time Formula 1 champion Max Verstappen has responded to Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff's claim that the era of the "ruthless" F1 driver is over. After Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli clinched his maiden world championship at the Mexican Grand Prix last weekend, Wolff used the 20-year-old as an example of a new kind of champion. "This notion of win at all costs, selfish, opportunistic, ruthless for your own benefit, that model of racing driver has died," Wolff said. "We have a new champion that represents values like humility, like integrity, loyalty, respect, being himself. Should be a role model for many other young drivers in junior formulas. And should be a role model for the few entitled ones in Formula 1, the endless moaners on the radio, the ones that complain, the ones that crash." Wolff did not name any drivers, but Verstappen and two-time champion Fernando Alonso were asked for their views during the drivers' press conference at Interlagos. Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing "I mean, everyone is entitled to their opinion, right? I have nothing else to say, really," Verstappen said. "Every person is different anyway. I think that’s what is good for Formula 1, because if everyone has the same personality, it’s very boring." Alonso was invited to share his thoughts on Wolff's comments, but he refused. Verstappen was more expansive when the subject turned to his own radio messages, which have often featured complaints about the car this season. "With shifts or whatever that you hear me complain about, it’s just because I’m never satisfied, because I think always certain things can be better, and I always try to fine-tune or find improvements," the Dutchman explained. "So if you hear it as complaining or whatever, it’s more for me to make sure that the team is always looking into details to try and find more lap time because I know there is more lap time in it." Verstappen sits second in the drivers' standings heading into the Brazilian Grand Prix. To read more Motorsport.com articles visit our website .

item.title: IBF orders Osleys Iglesias to face Malik Zinad
item.description: After a two-fight 2026 campaign that saw him win and defend the IBF super middleweight title in merciless fashion, Cuban menace Osleys Iglesias is on the clock for his inaugural mandatory defense against Malik Zinad . You know how I made a big deal about how Artur Subkhankulov, who fights Andy Cruz for the vacant lightweight belt in a few weeks , was a genuinely capable fighter and not just another of the IBF’s endless conveyor belt of mediocre non-contenders who somehow tumbled up the rankings? Zinad (24-1, 18 KO) is not that kind of exception. He has the ignominy of being Dmitry Bivol’s only stoppage win in the latter’s last 13 fights and his two wins in the last two years came above the 168-pound limit against nothing competition. It’s not even clear to me why or how they’re ordering this. The IBF usually keeps the top one or two slots empty until someone wins an official final eliminator, which is the case here; their rankings go Blank, Blank, Kevin Lele Sadjo, and then Zinad. How that translates to “mandatory challenger Malik Zinad” is beyond me, which might just be a case of me slacking off on my research into Sanctioning Body Lore. In my defense, extended exposure causes Necronomicon-like effects and I don’t need more eyes on the inside. I’ve sent them a message asking for more details and will update this piece if I receive a response. Giving someone a top-5 ranking in a division he’s never been part of is some WBA crap, especially when his only notable win is beating Jerome Pampellone. That said, their 168-pound rankings are just kind of a trainwreck in general. After the quartet above it’s Oliver Zaren (just lost to Iglesias), Bektemir Melikuziev (WBA mandatory), and Nikita Zon (just lost to Jaime Munguia). A bit of spring cleaning wouldn’t go amiss. At least it keeps Iglesias (16-0, 15 KO) busy. His prospects for unification, already slim by virtue of being a terrifying knockout machine with limited financial support and presence in the public eye, are now zero until Canelo runs out of other options. All he can really do at this point is puff up the highlight reel.

With an elite defense, the biggest thing for Denver's front office to focus on is helping out Bo Nix. While they could go after Jonathan Taylor, as the rumors lately have indicated, there is another area they could look to upgrade: the offensive line. ESPN's Seth Walder is urging the Broncos to do just that with a bold trade for Philadelphia Eagles three-time Pro Bowl offensive guard Landon Dickerson. Broncos urged to trade for Landon Dickerson from Eagles "Who should they target? Eagles G Landon Dickerson," Walder writes. "One of the reasons quarterback Bo Nix had early career success was that he played behind one of the best offensive lines. This season, that hasn't been the case with the Broncos ranking 20th in pass-block win rate." With the Broncos' offensive line playing below expectations this season, it would make sense to consider adding to the OL in some capacity. Walder believes Dickerson, the veteran lineman from the Eagles who helped them win a Super Bowl over the Chiefs in 2024, could be an option for the Broncos. MORE : Jayden Daniels snaps unbelievable drought with Commanders' win over Eagles Dickerson is a left guard, so he could take over for Ben Powers and help raise the floor of this offense, if Denver's front office believes Dickerson's struggles are behind him. Since returning from injured reserve, he has looked a lot better for the Eagles. With Philadelphia at 2-6, someone like Dickerson is very much available for trade. He's a three-time Pro Bowler and Super Bowl champion, and while his contract gets expensive, the Broncos could get out of his deal if they don't like how he plays. This could be a low-cost, low-risk move for the Broncos that could be a major improvement for the OL if it works out. Protecting Nix should be their top priority, and adding Dickerson could do just that. The New York Knicks made a roster adjustment a few weeks ago, signing former Los Angeles Lakers forward Dalton Knecht to a two-way contract. Knecht made his Knicks debut last night, scoring 10 points on 4-for-6 shooting with seven rebounds. However, he posted a plus-minus of -9 when on the floor. A roster spot opened up for Knecht after the Knicks waived Kevin McCullar Jr., who signed a two-way contract with the Toronto Raptors on Thursday, per Blake Murphy of Sportsnet.ca . McCullar spent his first two professional seasons with the Knicks, averaging 2.2 points and 1.4 rebounds in 7.4 minutes per game. He was the 56th overall pick in the 2024 NBA Draft out of Kansas. item.title: LaMelo Ball Saw Something From the Bench That Changed the Game
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect LaMelo Ball had a plan before he returned to the floor in Houston. Watching from the bench, he studied how the game was unfolding and identified opportunities he believed he could use. When Minnesota needed someone to take control of a close fourth quarter, he was ready. “I just seen the game from the side, and I’m like, ‘Oh yeah, when I get back in, I know what I can do,’” Ball said afterward . What followed helped turn a difficult night into Minnesota’s most impressive win since Anthony Edwards underwent knee surgery. Ball scored 12 of his 20 points in the fourth quarter as the Timberwolves beat the Rockets 117-107 on Wednesday. During one four-minute stretch, he scored or assisted on 15 consecutive Minnesota points, taking the Wolves from three behind to four ahead. The performance gave Chris Finch something he had been asking his new point guard to provide: aggression that creates good possessions for the entire team. Nov 2, 2026; Minneapolis, Minnesota, USA; Minnesota Timberwolves guard LaMelo Ball (1) smiles as he answers questions following the win over the Milwaukee Bucks at Target Center. Mandatory Credit: Bruce Kluckhohn-Imagn Images “You put the ball in his hands down the stretch, and he just made the right play after the right play after the right play,” Finch said . Ball kept trusting his teammates, Finch explained, and those teammates trusted the next pass. That sequence of decisions allowed Minnesota to pull away from a Houston team that entered the night 7-1. It was a different assignment from the one Ball initially took on after arriving in Minnesota. Finch said Ball began the season concentrating on setting up teammates and developing chemistry. His connection with Edwards formed quickly, and he was comfortable facilitating while the Wolves’ leading scorer handled a substantial share of the offense. Edwards’ absence changed what Minnesota needed. “Ant goes out, we need him to be more aggressive in all the ways,” Finch said. “Obviously playmaking, but also for himself to score.” Finding that balance has been uneven. Ball’s early Minnesota performances included productive stretches interrupted by turnovers, difficult shooting nights and foul trouble. Against Houston, he still finished with seven turnovers. His closing performance showed how much influence he can have when his scoring threat and passing work together. Ball did not offer a detailed tactical explanation afterward. He described letting the game come to him and using what he had observed while watching. The result was an offense that could generate its next opportunity without requiring him to finish every possession himself. Jonathan Kuminga supplied two important corner threes late.
